'''''Erythrina fusca''''' is a species of [[Flowering plant|flowering]] [[tree]] in the [[legume]] family, ''[[Fabaceae]]''.<ref name=POWO>{{cite web |url= https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:494431-1 |title= Erythrina fusca Lour. |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=n.d. |website=Plants of the World Online |publisher=The Trustees of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew |access-date=July 10, 2025}}</ref><ref name=COL>{{cite web |url= https://www.catalogueoflife.org/data/taxon/6GRZX |title= Erythrina fusca Lour. |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=n.d. |website=Catalogue of Life |publisher=Species 2000 |access-date=July 10, 2025}}</ref> It is known by many common names, including '''purple coraltree''', '''gallito''', '''bois immortelle''', '''bucayo''', and the more ambiguous '''"bucare"''' and  '''"coral bean"'''. ''E. fusca'' has the widest distribution of any ''Erythrina'' species; it is the only one found in both the [[New World|New]] and [[Old World]]. It grows on coasts and along rivers in tropical [[Asia]], [[Oceania]], the [[Mascarene Islands]], [[Madagascar]], [[Africa]], and the [[Neotropical realm|Neotropics]].<ref name="RNGR">{{cite web|url=http://www.rngr.net/Publications/ttsm/Folder.2003-07-11.4726/PDF.2004-03-03.5508/file |format=[[PDF]] |first=Nancy Barrera |last=Marín |title=''Erythrina fusca'' Lour. |work=Tropical Tree Seed Manual |publisher=Reforestation, Nurseries & Genetics Resources |date=2003-01-01 |access-date=2009-03-29 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090116103644/http://www.rngr.net/Publications/ttsm/Folder.2003-07-11.4726/PDF.2004-03-03.5508/file |archive-date=January 16, 2009 }}</ref>

The easy-to-grow and attractive flowering tree is cultivated as an ornamental shade and hedge plant. It is a common shade tree in [[cacao plantation]]s. It attracts [[hummingbirds]], which [[Pollinator|pollinate]] its flowers.

''E. fusca'' is the official flower of the [[Venezuela]]n state of [[Trujillo (state)|Trujillo]].
<!-- OrnitolColomb3:7. -->

==Description==
''E. fusca'' is a [[deciduous]] tree with spiny [[Bark (botany)|bark]] and light orange [[flower]]s. Its legume pods reach {{convert|20|cm|in}} in length and contain dark brown [[seed]]s. The seeds are [[Buoyancy|buoyant]], allowing them [[Drift seed|disperse across oceans]].<ref>{{cite journal |url=https://www.seabean.com/newsletters/vol07-1.pdf |title=Notes On The Ocean Dispersal of Coral Beans |first=Wayne P. |last=Armstrong |journal=The Drifting Seed |date=May 2001 |volume=7 |issue=1 |pages=5–6}}</ref>  The tree is highly adapted to coastal conditions, tolerant of both flooding and [[Halophyte|salinity]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fao.org/ag/AGP/AGPC/doc/Publicat/Gutt-shel/x5556e0b.htm |title=Erythrina Species - Pantropical Multipurpose Tree Legumes |first=D.L. |last=Kass |work=Forage Tree Legumes in Tropical Agriculture |publisher=[[Food and Agriculture Organization]] |access-date=2009-03-29 |archive-date=2013-06-16 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130616234059/http://www.fao.org/ag/AGP/AGPC/doc/publicat/gutt-shel/x5556e0b.htm }}</ref>

Like many other species in the genus ''[[Erythrina]]'', ''E. fusca'' contains [[Toxin|toxic]] [[alkaloid]]s which have been utilized for medicinal value but are [[poison]]ous in larger amounts. The most common alkaloid is [[erythraline]], which is named for the genus.

==As food==
The buds and leaves are eaten as a vegetable. In [[Thailand]] ''Erythrina fusca'' ({{langx|th|ทองหลาง}}) leaves are often eaten in [[Miang kham]] ({{langx|th|เมี่ยงคำ}}).<ref>[ftp://smc.ssk.ac.th/intranet/Research_AntioxidativeThaiVegetable/www/Native_veg/v142.html ทองหลาง]{{dead link|date=May 2025|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref>
